achieve_passing_justification: The project holds the passing badge: https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/13330
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md lists what a pull request needs: passing tests with new tests for new code, no coverage drop, a clean SpotBugs and Sonar run, the Google Java Style enforced by Spotless, and a DCO sign-off on every commit. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
dco_justification: Every commit must carry a Signed-off-by line under the Developer Certificate of Origin (https://developercertificate.org/), explained in https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin. The dco workflow fails a pull request with a commit whose sign-off does not match its author: https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/.github/workflows/dco.yml
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents the single-maintainer model: how changes are proposed, who decides, how decisions and disagreements are recorded on issues and pull requests. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
code_of_conduct_justification: Contributor Covenant in the standard location: https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md has a table of roles (maintainer, release manager, security contact, code owner, contributor), who holds each and what they must do. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
access_continuity_justification: A successor is designated in the maintainer's GitHub account settings and can archive the repository or transfer it to their own account or an organization, then manage issues, merge pull requests and push release tags. Releases are signed with keyless cosign through GitHub Actions OIDC, so no private key has to be handed over, and the whole build and release process runs in GitHub Actions. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
bus_factor_justification: The project has one maintainer, who wrote almost all non-bot commits in the last year, so the bus factor is 1. GOVERNANCE.md says so and describes how a contributor can become a co-maintainer. The continuity plan covers the loss of the maintainer in the meantime. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#adding-maintainers
documentation_roadmap_justification: Planned work for the coming releases is tracked in GitHub milestones, referenced from GOVERNANCE.md as the roadmap. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/milestones
documentation_security_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md states what users can and cannot expect from the software's security, linked from SECURITY.md. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md
documentation_current_justification: AGENTS.md requires README.md, .env.example and docs/ to change in the same pull request as operator-visible behavior or configuration, and the docs site is versioned and deployed from each release tag. Known documentation defects are tracked as issues. https://devops-thiago.github.io/ThrillhouseBot/ https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/AGENTS.md#changelog-and-docs
documentation_achievements_justification: The README badge row links the OpenSSF Best Practices badge, OpenSSF Scorecard, CI, coverage and SonarCloud quality gate. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The docs site is built with Astro Starlight, which ships accessible defaults (landmarks, skip link, keyboard navigation, language attribute); a Lighthouse 12.8.2 accessibility audit on 2026-10-15 scored 99 on the home and Getting started pages and 98 on Configuration. The dashboard sets the page language and scored 100 on Overview and Sessions and 94 on Costs and Tokens. The remaining findings (two unlabeled selects, heading order, a redundant logo alt) are tracked in https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/issues/1123
internationalization_justification: The bot's review comments and the dashboard are written in English and their strings are not externalized for translation. The users are developers reviewing pull requests on GitHub.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub (repository, issues, releases, GHCR) and GitHub Pages (docs). The project stores no passwords for external users; dashboard sign-in in the software uses GitHub OAuth.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is supported, and the README documents the upgrade: read the CHANGELOG section, pull the new image and restart. Each release's notes start with what changes for an existing installation (settings, defaults, database). The database schema is updated in place on startup. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/README.md#upgrading https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability reports were resolved in the last 12 months; the repository has no published security advisories. SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters in the advisory and CHANGELOG unless they ask to stay anonymous. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents the steps from acknowledgement within 48 hours through triage, a private fix in the advisory fork, a patch release, publishing the advisory and CVE, and reporter credit. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
coding_standards_justification: Java follows the Google Java Style Guide; the dashboard is TypeScript in strict mode; workflows are checked by actionlint and shellcheck. Contributions must comply. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-style
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Spotless formats Java with google-java-format on every compile, and the CI format job runs spotless:check, which fails on any unformatted file. There are no formatter exceptions in the code. actionlint (with shellcheck) runs on every pull request. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/pom.xml https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: The project has no C or C++ sources and no make-based native build. The native executable is produced by GraalVM native-image from Java bytecode through Maven, so CC, CFLAGS and LDFLAGS do not apply.
build_preserve_debug_justification: maven-compiler-plugin compiles with debug information (-g) by default and nothing strips it from the jars. Debug symbols for the native executable can be requested with -Dquarkus.native.debug.enabled=true. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/pom.xml
build_non_recursive_justification: The Java application is a single-module Maven project with one dependency graph. The dashboard (frontend/) and the docs site (website/) are independent npm projects with no cross-dependencies. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/pom.xml
build_repeatable_justification: pom.xml sets project.build.outputTimestamp, and two clean ./mvnw package builds a minute apart produce byte-identical jars (the whole target/quarkus-app tree and the project jar have the same SHA-256). The claim covers the JVM build artifacts; the GraalVM native executable and the container images are not claimed to be bit-for-bit reproducible. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/pom.xml
installation_common_justification: The software is installed as a container image from GHCR with docker compose up -d and removed with docker compose down. Signed binary tarballs are attached to each release. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/README.md#quick-start
installation_standard_variables_justific: The software ships as container images and a single self-contained binary in a release tarball. There is no installer that writes into a filesystem prefix, so DESTDIR and similar conventions do not apply.
installation_development_quick_justifica: With JDK 25 the Maven wrapper is enough: ./mvnw verify runs the tests against in-memory H2 with no external services, and ./mvnw quarkus:dev starts dev mode. The dashboard needs npm ci. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development-setup https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/README.md#development
external_dependencies_justification: Dependencies are declared in pom.xml (Maven), frontend/package.json and website/package.json with lock files. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/pom.xml https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/frontend/package.json https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/website/package.json
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot checks Maven, both npm projects and GitHub Actions weekly; Dependency Review blocks pull requests that add high or critical advisories; Trivy scans the source tree on every pull request, the main images after each build, and the latest images weekly; OpenSSF Scorecard runs OSV checks. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/.github/workflows/security-scan.yml
updateable_reused_components_justificati: All reused components come through Maven and npm with lock files, with no vendored copies, so Dependabot or a version bump updates them. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/pom.xml
interfaces_current_justification: The code targets Java 25 and current Quarkus. A clean compile with -Dmaven.compiler.showDeprecation=true reports no deprecated API use in the project code, and SonarCloud shows no open deprecated-API issues (java:S1874).
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The CI test job runs the JUnit suite, including about 30 @QuarkusTest classes that boot the application, on every pull request and push to main, develop and release branches, and reports results and coverage to Codecov and SonarCloud. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: Of the 316 fix commits on main in the six months to 2026-10-15 that changed src/main, 306 also changed src/test (97%). CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests that prove a fix.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: JaCoCo line coverage is 99.7% (Codecov). ./mvnw verify fails below 80% and Codecov's patch target holds new code to the project level. https://codecov.io/gh/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/codecov.yml
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: all tests pass and new code has tests, enforced by Codecov patch coverage and the SonarCloud quality gate. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#before-you-open-a-pull-request
tests_documented_added_justification: The change-proposal instructions require tests for new code. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#before-you-open-a-pull-request
warnings_strict_justification: SpotBugs runs at effort Max and threshold Low and fails the build on any finding; exclusions need a written justification. The SonarCloud quality gate fails on new issues. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/pom.xml https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/config/spotbugs-exclude.xml
implement_secure_design_justification: Least privilege, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation and economy of mechanism are applied as described in https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md#secure-design-principles
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Security mechanisms use HMAC-SHA256 (webhook and notification signatures), SHA-256 fingerprints, RS256 for GitHub App authentication and SecureRandom for tokens. No MD5, SHA-1 or other weak algorithm is used.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The algorithms are fixed by the protocols the bot implements: GitHub signs webhooks only with HMAC-SHA256 and requires RS256 for App JWTs. The bot follows them and cannot offer a choice. TLS cipher selection is left to the JDK.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: All credentials (GitHub App private key, webhook secret, OAuth client secret, model API key, notification secret) are read from environment variables, separate from application.properties, the database and logs. They can come from an env file or a secret manager and are replaced with a restart, without recompiling. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/README.md#responsible-use-and-security
crypto_used_network_justification: Outbound connections (GitHub, the model endpoint, the notification webhook) use HTTPS by default, and the notification webhook rejects http:// unless explicitly allowed. The inbound listener is plain HTTP on port 8080 by default and is documented to sit behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy; Quarkus TLS can be enabled instead, but plain HTTP is not off by default.
crypto_tls12_justification: TLS is provided by the JDK 25 JSSE stack, which supports TLS 1.2 and 1.3 and disables TLS 1.0 and 1.1 by default.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The bot uses the JDK and Vert.x default TLS settings, which verify certificates and host names. There is no custom TrustManager, HostnameVerifier or trust-all setting. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md#common-weaknesses-countered
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Tokens and API keys are sent only in requests over HTTPS connections, and the certificate is verified during the TLS handshake before any request header is sent.
signed_releases_justification: Release images and binary tarballs are signed with cosign (keyless, Sigstore) by the release workflow and carry build-provenance attestations. The README explains how to verify them with cosign and gh attestation verify. No private key is stored on the distribution sites. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/README.md#verifying-a-release
version_tags_signed_justification: v0.6.8 and v0.6.9 are signed with the maintainer's SSH key, but v0.7.0, v0.7.1 and the earlier tags are not. docs/RELEASING.md now requires git tag -s for every release and explains how to verify a tag. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/docs/RELEASING.md#verifying-a-release-tag
input_validation_justification: Webhooks are authenticated by HMAC before parsing and parsed into typed records; event types, commands and dashboard parameters are matched against fixed lists, page sizes are clamped, and configuration is range-checked at startup. Untrusted PR text is fenced before it reaches the model. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md#common-weaknesses-countered
hardening_justification: Dashboard cookies are HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax; untrusted text is wrapped in per-call random fences; the native binary is installed read-only (0555) in a minimal image run as a non-root user, and the distroless variant has no shell. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md
assurance_case_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md gives the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure design principles applied and the common weaknesses countered with pointers to the code. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL scans Java and TypeScript on pull requests and weekly, SonarCloud's security rules gate every pull request, and SpotBugs runs at maximum effort. https://github.com/devops-thiago/ThrillhouseBot/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The software is written in Java and TypeScript, which are memory-safe.
